item.title: Puffy:
item.content:encoded:
I was suitably spooked out by this tale. The physical description of the deflating creature/guy in the orange coat with the massive smile and the pearly white crooked teeth is very disturbing to picture. Same for the situation with the trucks on the side of the road and the guys yelling and waving. Your redactions also all serve the scary vibe. Where does she work? Why can't she even tell us what it is? Why does she say she went back through twice but only says what happened once?
Characterization of the woman is great, just enough that I can get a sense of who she is. Only thing that I'm not too sure on is the characterization of the husband. Partway through, wife says husband plays the skeptic, but at the end she says that he claims to have seen Bigfoot. Is he a real horror enthusiast for fun's sake, a real believer, or is he a skeptic? Although honestly if you did that intentionally it's probably a good idea because it made the story a little more unsettling.
Thanks for posting.

item.title: The Shape of a Gun:
item.content:encoded: Just popping in to shout my appreciation! After the first couple Series of SCPs I recognized the subtext of the Foundation as slavers, racists (pure human superiority) and tyrants (unelected O5s control the world) - Nazis, in a word. So happy to see them fought against! This tale just lights me up with excitement! I figure it should have at least one 2020 comment. Thank you for this!

item.title: Lily's Proposal: Thoughts
item.content:encoded:
I'm really nobody important, but I figured I'd give my thoughts on a two-year-old article anyway. Just to preface, I really like this article, but it seems a bit uncharacteristic. Unless the anomaly affects everyone's minds to make them at peace about the end of the world, wouldn't the Foundation try to counteract the end of the world. I mean, something being inevitable hasn't stopped them from at least attempting it before.

Also, I think that a bit more should be added (mainly who discovered it and how) but other than that I like the brevity and self-explanation of the article.

item.content:encoded: III

I don't exactly feel this fits the whole Rat's Nest ethos, if you will. From what I've seen, RN is less about the end of the universe and more about the Universe changing fundamentally (in a way that it might as well have ended for the people in it.) This, however, is a full-on, YK-style THE END BLAARMMFFF and it's not for me. I dunno, it kinda works, but I feel like it doesn't exactly fit the canon.

Novote.

item.title: SCP-4576:
item.content:encoded: Oh. Well, Lana had the scarecrow as a doll as a kid and she accidentally lost it. The doll came to life and tried to kill her out of revenge because it believed she abandoned it but the childhood home videos showed that it was just a misunderstanding, so the scarecrow went outside and lit itself on fire out of guilt and shame. Perhaps I could have shown that better…
